papers.version_note: arXiv:2305.11518v2 [quant-ph] 25 Jan 2024; a Perspective, not a research paper with theorems or new measurements. The text layer prints exponents flat (for example 10−18 for ten to the minus eighteen).
papers.what_it_is: A Perspective surveying quantum sensing technologies (atom interferometers, clocks, optomechanics, superconducting and spin sensors) and their use in neutrino, EDM, fundamental-symmetry, dark matter, dark energy and detector physics.

assertions.value: The authors define quantum sensors, for the purposes of the paper, as any device whose measurement capabilities are enabled by the ability to manipulate or read out its quantum states.
quotes: we will consider as quantum sensors any device whose measurement capabilities are enabled by our ability to manipulate and / or read out its quantum states
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors define the term for the paper in Section 2.

assertions.value: The authors divide quantum sensors into two categories: low-energy sensors, where the probed energy scale matches the sensor's own energy levels (typically at or below the eV scale), and sensors that form part of a larger system for high energy particle physics, with energies above the keV scale.
quotes: Quantum sensors fall naturally into two categories, those - at low energies - where the energy scale being probed is commensurate with those of the energy levels of the sensor itself, typically at or below the eV scale

those where quantum systems form part of a larger system, in which their specifics enhance existing methods or enable novel types of detectors better suited to high energy particle physics (HEP), with energies above the keV scale.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own classification in Section 2.

assertions.value: The authors state that the paper discusses a selection of key areas where quantum sensors can have a significant impact, and does not claim to be exhaustive; its prime focus is neutrino properties, fundamental symmetries including the equivalence principle, dark matter and dark energy.
quotes: In this Perspective we discuss a selection of key areas where quantum sensors can have a significant impact
with prime focus on neutrino properties, fundamental symmetries including the equivalence principle, dark matter and dark energy.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own scope.

assertions.value: The authors state that quantum mechanics is potentially used in detector technologies to go beyond measurement limits such as the standard quantum limit and shot noise limits, with a view to approaching the Heisenberg limit.
quotes: to go beyond different measurement limits3,4, e.g. the standard quantum limit and shot noise limits of measurement uncertainty, with a view to approaching the fundamental Heisenberg limit imposed by the uncertainty relations5

assertions.value: The authors state that the already high sensitivity of quantum sensors can be enhanced further when they are used as an ensemble of entangled sub-systems or prepared so that decoherence of their quantum states is minimized.
quotes: The already very high sensitivity of these systems to interactions can be enhanced even further when they are not considered in isolation but as an ensemble of entangled sub-systems

assertions.value: The authors state that the large-baseline terrestrial atom interferometers AION, MAGIS and MIGA are under development or prototyping, and that once operational at the appropriate large scale they will be highly sensitive to low-frequency gravitational waves and to ultra-light dark matter.
quotes: A terrestrial large baseline atom interferometer (vertical, such as AION25 or MAGIS26 or horizontal, such as MIGA27, all three under development or prototyping for larger baselines)
will, once operational at the appropriate large scale, be highly sensitive not only to low-frequency gravitational waves, but also to ultra-light dark matter28

assertions.value: The authors state that breaking Cooper pairs in a superconductor requires O(10−3 eV), whereas the semiconductor bandgap of O(1eV ∼ 1000nm) means low energy photons can only be detected with very poor energy resolution.
quotes: the bandgap of O(1eV ∼ 1000nm) entails that low energy photons can only be detected with very poor energy resolution
the corresponding excitation process in superconductors (the breaking of Cooper pairs) requires O(10−3 eV)

assertions.value: The authors state that arrays of transition edge sensors, superconducting nanowire single photon detectors and kinetic inductance detectors are mature technologies in standard use, such as astrophysical imaging detectors for microwave photons.
quotes: Arrays of sensors are mature technologies in standard use such as astrophysical imaging detectors for microwave photons.

assertions.value: The authors state that the low coupling of optomechanical sensors to their environment, and thus their low decoherence, allows them once in their vibrational ground state to be sensitive at the single phonon level.
quotes: The low coupling of these sensors to their environment (and thus their low decoherence) allows such sensors - once in their vibrational ground state - to be sensitive at the single phonon level.

assertions.value: The authors state that atomic clocks have frequency uncertainties at the level of 10−18 or less, and that transient or oscillatory interactions would affect their clock frequency.
quotes: Transient or oscillatory interactions affecting highly-precise atomic clocks (with frequency uncertainties at the level of 10−18 or less39), will affect their clock frequency

assertions.value: The authors state that networks of clocks are sensitive to local periodic or transient changes and to slow drifts of fundamental constants, and are more sensitive the larger the network, since spurious local causes are easily identified.
quotes: networks of clocks are not only highly sensitive to both such local (periodic or transient) changes as to slow drifts of fundamental constants, but are all the more sensitive the larger the size of the network is, as spurious local causes are easily identified.

assertions.value: The authors state that, because different atomic clocks and the single candidate nuclear clock (thorium) have different systematics and couplings, continent- or globe-spanning networks of many heterogeneous clocks would be ultimately sensitive and could determine the directionality of domain-wall-produced perturbations.
quotes: dedicated networks spanning continents or the globe, and composed of a large number of heterogeneous clocks would not only represent an ultimately sensitive system, but would also allow determining the directionality of e.g. domain wall-produced perturbations40.

assertions.value: The authors state that promising developments to enhance sensitivity build on quantum squeezing, on entangling ensembles of quantum systems for distributed quantum sensing, and on arrays and networks of linked detectors.
quotes: a number of particularly promising developments build on quantum squeezing41
on entangling ensembles of quantum systems for distributed quantum sensing42

assertions.value: The authors caution that other improvements, namely more systems, longer coherence times, lower temperature and higher control of application-specific systems, will likely lead to more straightforward initial gains than squeezing, entanglement and networks.
quotes: It must be pointed out however that a number of other areas of possible improvement, such as increasing the number and coherence times, decreasing the temperature, and achieving higher control of possibly application-specific systems will likely lead to more straightforward initial gains.
assertions.reader_inference: This is a stated limit on the case for entanglement-based sensing, offered without evidence in the paper.

assertions.value: The authors state that quantum computing ideas are discussed in particle physics, for example for processing huge data sets and for improving trigger or data reconstruction performance in future collider experiments such as the high luminosity upgrade of the Large Hadron Collider.
quotes: quantum computing ideas are also discussed in particle physics, for example with processing huge data sets or in improving trigger or data reconstruction performance in future collider experiments like the high luminosity upgrade of the Large Hadron Collider47
assertions.reader_inference: The paper gives this one sentence to quantum computing and presents no result; it is a pointer to a cited review.

assertions.value: The authors report, citing a review, that for three neutrino species the largest mass squared difference is constrained to about 2 × 10−3 eV2 and the smaller one is (7.53 ± 0.18) × 10−5 eV2, and that the lightest neutrino mass is expected to be about 10−8 times the electron mass.

the lightest neutrino mass is expected to be about 10−8 times the value of the electron mass

assertions.value: The authors state that the Particle Data Group combined cosmological bound on the neutrino mass sum is less than 0.12 eV in the usual ΛCDM model, with individual measurements typically bounded by about 0.5 eV.
quotes: Cosmology gives a bound on the mass sum with the Particle Data Group combined value 54, ∑ mν < 0.12 eV in context of the usual ΛCDM model of cosmology with individual measurements typically bounded by about 0.5 eV.

quotes: There are hints for charge-parity, CP, violation in the neutrino sector at the level of 1-2 σ 54.

quotes: then their masses are expected to be ∼ Λ2ew/M where Λew is the electroweak scale 246 GeV and M is a large mass scale, typically about 1016 GeV.

assertions.value: The authors state that, because an electric dipole moment is proportional to the particle's spin, which is odd under time reversal, any finite electric dipole moment violates time reversal invariance and, through CPT, violates CP.
quotes: Hence any finite electric dipole moment corresponds to a violation of time reversal invariance, T, symmetry and, through the fundamental symmetry of combined charge, parity and time reversal invariance, CPT, to a violation of CP.
assertions.certainty_reason: Standard symmetry argument stated by the authors in Section 3.

assertions.value: The authors report the best present neutron EDM measurement as |dn| < 3.0 × 10−26 ecm, which constrains strong CP violation induced by gluon topological effects, with the QCD θ parameter less than 10−10.
